🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Name the members of a family in English.
- Use possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their).
- Use the possessive 's to show that something belongs to someone.
- Describe your own family in a short paragraph.

🔍 Warm-up
Look at this sentence: "This is Ali. This is his sister. Her name is Mona."
Notice "his" and "her". Why do we say his for Ali but her for Mona? By the end of the lesson you will explain it easily.

I. Family vocabulary

📘 Rule (vocabulary)
The family is a group of people related to each other. Key words:
- Parents: mother (mum), father (dad).
- Children: son, daughter, brother, sister.
- Wider family: grandmother (grandma), grandfather (grandpa), uncle, aunt, cousin, nephew, niece.
- Married life: husband, wife.

📏 Useful groups
- grandparents = grandmother + grandfather.
- parents = mother + father.
- siblings = brothers and sisters together.

✏️ Worked example
My mother's mother is my grandmother. My father's brother is my uncle. My uncle's son is my cousin.

👀 Note
"Cousin" is the same word for a boy or a girl in English. There is no separate word like in Arabic or French.

II. Possessive adjectives

<text x="430" y="61" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#ffffff">Possessive adjective</text>

<text x="320" y="282" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">Ali and his book. Leila and her dress. The dog wags its tail.</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📘 Rule (grammar)
Possessive adjectives show who owns something. They come BEFORE a noun.
📏 Forms
- I → my
- you → your
- he → his
- she → her
- it → its
- we → our
- they → their

✏️ Worked examples
- This is my book.
- Is that your bag?
- Karim loves his dog.
- Leila visits her grandmother.
- We clean our room.
- The children do their homework.

🛠️ Method: choosing the right possessive
Step 1 — Ask: WHO is the owner?
Step 2 — Match the owner to the pronoun (he, she, they...).
Step 3 — Use the matching possessive (his, her, their...).
Example: The owner is Mona (she) → use "her": Mona and her friend.

⚠️ Common mistakes
- The possessive matches the OWNER, not the object. Ali and her book → Ali and his book (Ali is a boy).
- "your" (belonging to you) is different from "you're" (you are).
- "their" (belonging to them) is different from "there" (place) and "they're" (they are).
- "its" (belonging to it) has NO apostrophe. "it's" means "it is".

III. The possessive 's

[[FIG]]<svg viewBox="0 0 660 250" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<text x="330" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">'s or s' ?</text>
<rect x="20" y="45" width="195" height="90" rx="8" fill="#3b82f6" opacity="0.15" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="117" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Singular owner</text>
<text x="117" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">owner + 's</text>
<text x="117" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">Sami's bike</text>
<text x="117" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">the teacher's desk</text>
<rect x="232" y="45" width="195" height="90" rx="8" fill="#16a34a" opacity="0.15" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="329" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Plural ending in -s</text>
<text x="329" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">owner + '</text>
<text x="329" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">the students' books</text>
<text x="329" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">my parents' house</text>
<rect x="444" y="45" width="195" height="90" rx="8" fill="#e11d48" opacity="0.15" stroke="#e11d48" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="541" y="65" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="currentColor">Irregular plural</text>
<text x="541" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="currentColor">owner + 's</text>
<text x="541" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">the children's toys</text>
<text x="541" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" font-style="italic">the men's team</text>
<rect x="60" y="160" width="540" height="65" rx="8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
<text x="330" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" font-weight="bold">Do not confuse:</text>
<text x="330" y="201" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">boys (plural) · boy's bag (possessive) · the boy's happy (= the boy is happy)</text>
</svg>[[/FIG]]
📘 Rule (grammar)
To say that something belongs to a person, we add 's to the person's name or noun.
📏 Form
- owner + 's + thing owned
- Sami's bike, my sister's phone, the teacher's desk.

✏️ Worked examples
- This is Nour's pen. (the pen of Nour)
- My father's car is blue.
- The dog's tail is long.

📏 Special cases
1. Plural nouns already ending in -s: add only an apostrophe. the students' books, my parents' house.
2. Irregular plurals (no -s): add 's normally. the children's toys, the men's team.

🛠️ Method: 's or of?
For people and animals we usually use 's: Ahmed's brother.
For things we often use "of": the door of the house, the end of the film.

👀 Note
Do not confuse the possessive 's with the plural -s or with the verb "is".
- boys = more than one boy (plural).
- boy's = belonging to the boy (possessive).
- The boy's happy = The boy is happy (contraction).

IV. Describing your family
📏 Form (useful sentences)
- I have got + number + brothers/sisters.
- There are + number + people in my family.
- My + relative + is/works/lives...
- His/Her name is...

✏️ Worked paragraph
There are five people in my family: my parents, my two brothers and me. My father is a teacher and my mother is a nurse. My older brother's name is Yassine; he is sixteen. My younger brother is called Adam. We live in a small house in Nabeul. I love my family very much.

⚠️ More common mistakes
1. Word order: my brother older → my older brother.
2. Using "have" for people count is fine (I have two sisters), but not for age (I am twelve, not I have twelve).
3. Capital letters for family members' names: my sister Sara.

⭐ Recap
- Know the family words: mother, father, brother, sister, grandparents, uncle, aunt, cousin.
- Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, our, their) come before a noun and match the OWNER.
- Add 's to a person to show possession: Sami's book.
- Plural nouns ending in -s take only an apostrophe: the students' books.

📘 Language bank
Family: mother, father, parents, brother, sister, son, daughter, grandmother, grandfather, uncle, aunt, cousin, husband, wife.
Possessives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
Useful sentences: This is my family. / I have two sisters. / Her name is Sara. / This is my brother's room. / How many people are there in your family?

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Choose the correct possessive adjective.
1. This is Karim and this is (his / her) bike.
2. Leila loves (his / her) new dress.
3. We clean (our / their) classroom every Friday.
4. The dog wags (its / it's) tail.
5. My parents love (their / there) garden.

Exercise 2 — Add 's or an apostrophe correctly.
1. This is (Sami) ______ football.
2. That is my (sister) ______ phone.
3. These are the (students) ______ books. (many students)
4. The (children) ______ toys are on the floor.
5. My (father) ______ car is blue.

Exercise 3 — Write true sentences about your family.
1. How many people are there in your family?
2. Name one brother, sister or cousin and give one detail.
3. What is your favourite family activity?

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. his 2. her 3. our 4. its 5. their.
Exercise 2: 1. Sami's 2. sister's 3. students' 4. children's 5. father's.

🗣️ Speaking task
Bring or draw a small family tree. Present it to a partner: "This is my father. His name is... This is my sister. Her name is..." Use as many possessive words as you can (my, his, her, our, their).

👀 Extra note
Keep these three "s" ideas separate:
1. Plural: two boys (more than one).
2. Possessive: the boy's bag (belonging to the boy).
3. Contraction: The boy's happy (= the boy is happy).
And always remember: the possessive adjective matches the OWNER, so it is Karim and HIS bike, Leila and HER dress.

🌍 Real-life English
You use possessives every single day. When you point to your things, you say "This is my bag, that is his phone, these are their books." When you talk about your family, every sentence needs a possessive: "My father is a teacher, her name is Sara, our house is small." Practise by describing five things around you (my pen, my chair, my classmate's book) and five people in your family (my sister, my uncle's car). The more you notice these little words in real conversations, the more natural they become. Possessives are small, but they carry a lot of meaning: they tell the listener exactly who owns what.

📋 Summary
- Family words: parents (mother/father), children (son/daughter, brother/sister), grandparents, uncle, aunt, cousin, husband, wife.
- Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) come BEFORE a noun and always match the OWNER, not the object.
- Common confusions: your/you're, their/there/they're, its/it's — learn each pair carefully.
- The possessive 's shows that something belongs to a person: owner + 's + thing owned (Sami's bike).
- Plural nouns already ending in -s take only an apostrophe: the students' books, my parents' house.
- Irregular plurals (children, men) take 's normally: the children's toys.
- For people/animals we usually use 's (Ahmed's brother); for things we often use "of" (the door of the house).
- Useful pattern for describing your family: "There are + number + people in my family. My + relative + is/works/lives..."
